scope: Source-runtime Docker context stability across image preflight, create/start and owned cleanup; local actual daemon fault injection plus offline real CLI transport snapshot checks.

reproduced_before_fix.mechanism: A disposable named context changed after the last route-fingerprint check, immediately before start. Docker reread it and contacted an unreachable socket; cleanup became unconfirmed. The mutation was never replayed.

implementation: Default contexts bind the resolved explicit host and captured TLS environment instead of resolving a context name for each daemon command.
Named contexts use a private Docker-exported/imported snapshot, with copied metadata checked against the captured selection before dispatch.
Snapshots preserve context TLS/SSH settings and configured daemon HttpHeaders. Registry login/credential-helper and unrelated proxy/container settings are not copied into named snapshots.
Image inspection, create, acknowledged-ID start and active removal share the same connection. Journal recovery likewise shares one pinned connection across list/inspect/remove.
Existing host/route checks, container identity/name/label ownership, bounded deadlines, unknown-create uncertainty, no-replay rules and single-owner locks remain in force.
Normal snapshot cleanup occurs on success, preparation errors and execution errors. Private directories use 0700 and copied files 0600.
A thin fault-injection consumer changes only its disposable Docker configuration, never the operator configuration or unrelated containers.
verified: A named-context endpoint update immediately before start cannot redirect the acknowledged container to another daemon.
A private default-selection change immediately before start cannot redirect an implicit-context run.
A context update immediately before recovery listing cannot redirect the inspect/remove sequence.

Actual CLI export/import retains a synthetic TLS key and verification settings, SSH endpoint settings and daemon headers. Registry sentinel values are absent from snapshots; no remote daemon was contacted for these two checks.
Existing close, owner death, process-group death, input deadline and unreachable/late-create recovery drills pass with actual local Docker.
All nine full-worker checks pass, including six-operation SQL/JQ/chart/ImageMagick/generated-code workflow, private artifact provenance and output bounds.
Legacy fingerprint calculation remains byte-compatible; saved v1 ownership records recover without schema conversion.
Actual daemon test containers are gone after acceptance. The unrelated llm-cli-proxy container remains running.

runtime.synthetic_tls_certificate: Temporary self-signed certificate generated by OpenSSL; no user private key was used in actual acceptance.

migration.upgrade: Update the source package and restart the service normally. Existing installed worker images are unchanged and need no rebuild.
migration.rollback: Existing v1 journals remain readable by the earlier runtime, which retains its known context-reconfiguration race; stop work before reverting.

limitations: Real remote/SSH sessions, disconnects and daemon restart were not exercised. TLS/SSH checks verify real CLI snapshot configuration, not network authentication or remote execution.
DNS, SSH aliases, default-context external certificate-file changes and other routing changes outside Docker context selection retain separate acceptance scope.
A SIGKILLed owner can leave a private snapshot in OS temporary storage until the host retention policy removes it; normal completion/errors remove snapshots immediately.
Native Windows and frozen/installed app acceptance of this source change remain pending. No desktop build was performed.
Personal HTTPS VM, selected provider accounts, physical voice devices, escaped MCP descendants and historical unclassified PDF evidence remain separate open gates.
release_note: Release checksum manifest retained; previous DMG files are absent and were not rebuilt or reverified.
